title: Emotional Register
rationale: Chiefs of Staff can be moved either by fear of things falling through the cracks or by the promise of a smarter-run company, and that appeal can be pitched at their own competence or at the organization's collective performance, so crossing these gives four distinct emotional strategies.

title: Narrative Style
rationale: This map separates how directly the ad demonstrates the product's mechanics versus makes a case, from whether the hero of the story is the tool or the people using it, which shapes tone and format independent of the emotional pitch above.

title: Operating Record Value

y_axis.name: Visible Control vs Ambient Trust
y_axis.high_label: Quiet system of record, rarely opened

rationale: Specific to this category: the same searchable history can be sold as a proactive coordination tool that stops future drift or as an arbiter that settles 'who decided what' after the fact, and separately the product can be positioned as something leaders actively monitor versus infrastructure that just needs to exist and be trusted, and these two questions are independent of each other.

title: Tone of Voice
rationale: First-time budgeters respond to very different creative registers depending on whether the ad leads with feeling or logic, and separately whether it treats money with levity or gravity, and these two choices can combine independently (e.g. rational-but-playful vs emotional-but-serious).

title: Narrative Framing
rationale: Ads can foreground the app's mechanics or the user's broader life story, and independently can position the audience's future self as an aspirational ideal or ground the message in relatable present-day struggle, giving four distinct storytelling strategies.

title: Behaviour Change Mechanism
rationale: This is specific to a budgeting app's core value proposition: whether the pitch emphasizes the app's automatic categorization taking work off your hands versus empowering your own decision-making, and whether the underlying psychology sold is fear of loss/guilt or the pleasure of achieving savings goals, both of which are distinct product-truths that can be dialed independently.

title: Motivation Style
rationale: First-half-marathon runners can be sold on how the shoe makes them feel about themselves or on the concrete performance/outcome it delivers, and separately the story can center on becoming 'a runner' versus hitting a specific finish-line goal, and these two questions are independent of each other.

title: Proof Strategy
rationale: Beginners need reassurance that the shoe 'works', but that reassurance can be built either from engineering credibility (carbon plate, foam science) or from lived first-timer testimony, and independently the credibility source can be an authority figure or a community of peers like them.

title: Novice Runner Journey
rationale: This is specific to first-time half-marathoners: the ad can address the anxious, uncertain lead-up training period or the climactic race itself, and separately can appeal by easing a worry or by fueling a dream, giving four genuinely distinct creative territories unique to this audience's journey.

title: Emotional Register
rationale: CISO messaging can appeal to gut-level threat anxiety or earned confidence, and can frame stakes as personal (job/liability) or organizational (brand/regulatory standing); these two tensions independently shape tone and target the CISO's dual identity as both a professional and a steward of the business.

title: Proof Style
rationale: Beyond just what is said, how proof is delivered varies independently between explaining mechanics vs. making a persuasive case, and between quantitative evidence vs. illustrative storytelling, giving four distinct credibility strategies for a technical buyer.

title: Consolidation Value Frame
rationale: This product's core pitch is consolidation, but that can be sold as reducing complexity/tool sprawl or as achieving comprehensive coverage, and its payoff can be framed as day-to-day security operations efficiency or as regulatory/compliance assurance—these are the two product-specific tensions unique to a unified detection-response-compliance platform for regulated industries.

title: Emotional Register
rationale: Ads can motivate through relieving parental worry or through painting a positive future, and they can center the emotional payoff on the parent's own relief or on the child's experience — these are independent choices that produce very different tones.

title: Proof Strategy
rationale: Some parents are convinced by grade statistics and outcomes while others are swayed by tutor vetting and testimonials, and separately the ad can either walk through the mechanics of the service or push an emotional sales narrative — these two decisions don't determine each other.

title: Tutoring Fit Model
rationale: This is specific to tutoring marketplaces: parents differ in whether they want a rigorous, replicable teaching method or a uniquely matched tutor-personality fit, and independently whether they're shopping for a quick grade rescue or a sustained weekly mentorship — both are live, non-overlapping ad strategies for this brief.

title: Solitude vs Sensation
rationale: This audience alternates between wanting to vanish from the world with a partner/family and wanting a rich, story-worthy experience to relive and share, and separately the resort can be sold on calm restoration or on vivid sensory adventure (diving, reef color) - these two questions are independent and together map distinct creative territories from 'silent private villa' to 'vivid shared reef spectacle'.

title: Reason to Book
rationale: Since this is a once-a-year trip, the ad must justify the splurge either as a deserved reset from a hard year or as a rare chance to discover something new (reef, culture, self), and independently it can persuade via concrete proof (ratings, craftsmanship, specs of villas/spa) or via evocative, aspirational imagery - crossing these gives four distinct persuasive strategies.

title: Above and Below the Waterline
rationale: Specific to this product, the resort's dual identity as both a luxury land-based retreat (villas, spa) and an active reef-diving destination creates a genuine spatial tension, while separately guests can be positioned as either being cared for or as adventuring themselves, so a diving trip can be framed as pampered (guided, effortless) or exploratory (self-directed discovery) just as the villa/spa side can.

title: Emotional Register
rationale: Ads for time-pressed parents can lean into either a sincere or a light-hearted tone, and separately can center the emotional payoff on the parent's own relief versus the family's shared experience, giving four distinct emotional territories.

title: Proof Strategy
rationale: Whether the ad proves its promise through appetizing craft detail or through hard functional facts is independent of whether the credibility comes from the chef's expertise or from real families vouching for it, so this map separates 'what convinces' from 'who convinces'.

title: Mealtime Trade-off
rationale: This is specific to the product and audience: the ten-minute reheat can be framed as removing cooking effort entirely or as freeing time to redirect toward other tasks, and this is independent of whether the ad shows children kept out of the way or actively included in the mealtime moment.

title: Tone of Address
rationale: Platform engineers respond to both the visceral dread of 3am outages and the cold logic of system architecture, and separately can be reached through either dry technical gravity or knowing gallows humor about on-call life, so crossing how an ad feels emotionally with how it feels in register opens up distinct creative territories.

title: Proof Strategy
rationale: Ads can either show the product working (a live trace resolving an incident) or simply state a benefit, and independently can frame the payoff as personal (the engineer looks like a hero, sleeps at night) or organizational (the company saves money, hits SLAs), giving four distinct persuasive strategies for a technical buyer.

title: Observability Framing
rationale: This product has two genuinely distinct value pillars specific to the brief -- collapsing fragmented telemetry into one view versus pinpointing per-service spend -- and each can be pitched either as a tool for surviving incidents in the moment or as a tool for preventing cost and reliability problems before they happen, a distinction unique to this observability-plus-FinOps positioning.

title: Tone & Emotional Register
rationale: Ads for a scarcity-based dating app can either appeal to the head (efficiency, wasted time saved) or the heart (loneliness, hope for connection), and separately can deliver that appeal with sincere warmth or knowing humor about dating app fatigue; these two tonal choices vary independently and together map the emotional territory available to the brand voice.

title: Narrative Focus
rationale: Concepts can foreground the mechanism (curated weekly matches, the algorithm's discipline) or the human story of a user's dating life, and separately can center a single protagonist's journey or a broader social phenomenon among peers, giving four distinct storytelling strategies for the same core promise.

title: Value Proposition Framing (Category-Specific)

x_axis.name: Scarcity as Relief vs Scarcity as Discipline

rationale: This app's defining feature—limiting matches—can be sold as a relaxing escape from swiping burnout or as a serious commitment device that forces better dating behavior, and the brand can position itself as rebelling against dating app culture broadly or as simply a better way to do the thing users already believe in (dating itself), a tension unique to this product's contrarian mechanic within its category.

title: Emotional Register
rationale: Occasional donors respond to different emotional triggers, and separating tone (how it feels) from focus (who it's about) lets us explore concepts like an uplifting single-family success story versus a somber statistic-driven community-wide plea, without conflating the two.

title: Conversion Mechanics
rationale: Since the audience lacks a giving habit, this map isolates whether the ad tries to convert a single gift or seed recurring behavior, independent of whether it earns trust through emotional credibility or transparent, trackable proof of where money goes.

title: Water Infrastructure Framing
rationale: Specific to clean-water campaigns, this map separates whether the ad dwells on the deprivation itself versus the infrastructure that fixes it, and whether it frames water as an immediate survival need or a catalyst for broader downstream life improvements like school attendance or local business growth.
